Here's the full analysis of the **TayAndTos** project:

---

## Project Overview

A full-stack **hotel/room booking web application** called **Tay and Tos** (likely a hospitality business). It allows users to register, book rooms, and manage reservations, with admin capabilities. Live at `tayandtoscorporations.com`.

---

## Directory Structure

```
TayAndTos/
├── Backend/       # Node.js/Express API server (port 8080)
├── Frontend/      # React app (Create React App)
├── Database/      # SQLite database file
├── .git/
└── .backboard/    # IDE/agent config
```

---

## Backend (Node.js/Express, ES Modules)

| Layer | Files | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Entry | `server.js` | Express app, CORS, DB init, mounts routes |
| DB | `db.js` | MySQL2 pool + SQLite3 (both used), admin seed |
| Schema | `setup.sql` | Creates `tay-tos-db`, 3 tables: `users`, `bookings`, `guest_bookings` |
| Routes | `routes/users.js` | Signup, login, profile CRUD, forgot/reset password, admin user management |
| | `routes/bookings.js` | Booking CRUD, find by confirmation code, conflict detection |
| | `routes/guest_bookings.js` | Guest (non-registered) bookings CRUD |
| | `routes/email_routes.js` | Email sending endpoints |
| Auth | `middleware/auth.js` | JWT token verification |
| Email | `sevices/email_service.js` | SendGrid-based transactional emails (booking confirm, password reset, etc.) |
| | `config/sendgrid.js` | SendGrid client config |
| | `templates/` | HTML/text email templates |
| Utils | `utils/generate_code.js`, `utils/securityUtils.js` | Confirmation code generation, password reset tokens |

**Key dependencies:** Express 5, mysql2, sqlite3, bcrypt, jsonwebtoken, @sendgrid/mail, dotenv, validator, cors, nodemon (dev)

---

## Frontend (React 18, Create React App)

```
my-app/src/
├── App.js                 # Router setup (12 routes)
├── pages/                 # 12 page components
│   ├── Home_Page.jsx
│   ├── Login_Page.jsx
│   ├── Sign-up_Page.jsx
│   ├── Forgot_Password.jsx
│   ├── Reset_Password.jsx
│   ├── Book_Page.jsx
│   ├── Booking_Success_Page.jsx
│   ├── Find_Booking_Page.jsx
│   ├── Profile_Page.jsx
│   ├── Manage_Bookings.jsx
│   ├── Manage_Users.jsx
│   └── Learn_More.jsx
├── components/            # Header (admin/guest/user variants, desktop/mobile), Footer
├── component_css/         # Component-level stylesheets
├── pages_css/             # Page-level stylesheets
├── backend_services/      # API client layer (axios instances for auth, booking, email, etc.)
├── images/                # Room/venue photos
└── videos/                # Property walkthrough videos
```

**Key deps:** react 18, react-router-dom 6, axios, react-scripts 5, testing-library

---

## Database Schema

Three MySQL tables:

1. **`users`** — id, email, first/last name, phone, password_hash, admin flag, reset_token/expiry
2. **`bookings`** — id, user_id (FK→users), room, check-in/out dates, guests, status, confirmation_code
3. **`guest_bookings`** — Same as bookings but for unregistered users (stores guest name/email/phone directly)

Plus a SQLite database at `Database/tayandtos.db` (also connected but MySQL is the primary).

---

## API Endpoints

| Prefix | Key Endpoints |
|--------|--------------|
| `/users` | POST signup/login, GET profile, PUT profile/password, POST forgot/reset-password, admin: GET / DELETE users, find-by-email |
| `/bookings` | GET all, POST create, PUT/DELETE by ID, POST find (by code+email), PUT/DELETE by-confirmation-code |
| `/guest_bookings` | POST create, POST find, cancel-by-confirmation |
| `/email` | Send emails |
| `/health`, `/db-status` | Health checks |

---

## Notable Observations

- **Dual DB setup**: Uses both MySQL (primary via mysql2 pool) and SQLite (`db.js` exports both). The MySQL driver is the main one; SQLite is connected but seems secondary/redundant.
- **Typo**: Directory is named `sevices/` instead of `services/` (but imports work since they reference the actual path).
- **`.env` has a live SendGrid API key committed** — this is a security concern; it should be kept out of version control.
- **React app points to production URL** (`REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://tayandtoscorporations.com`) rather than localhost for dev.
- **Rich email system**: Full transactional email flow for signup confirmation, booking confirmation/update/cancellation, password reset.
- **Room conflict detection**: Both `bookings` and `guest_bookings` are checked for date overlaps.
- **Auth**: JWT-based with admin role support; some booking operations also allow unauthenticated access via confirmation code.

# Tay and Tos Accommodation

A full-stack room booking web application for Tay and Tos Accommodation in Ado-Ekiti, Nigeria. Users can browse rooms, create accounts, book rooms, and manage reservations. Administrators can manage users and bookings.

## System Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    User["Website Visitor"]
    User -->|HTTPS| React["React 18 Frontend (Create React App)"]
    
    React -->|HTTP API Requests| Express["Node.js / Express 5 Backend"]
    Express -->|Auth Middleware| Auth["JWT Authentication"]
    Express -->|Rate Limiting| Rate["express-rate-limit"]
    Express -->|Security Headers| Helmet["helmet"]
    Express -->|CORS| CORS["cors"]
    
    Auth -->|Protected Routes| Routes["Route Handlers"]
    Rate --> Routes
    Helmet --> Routes
    
    Routes --> MySQL["MySQL Database"]
    Routes --> SendGrid["SendGrid Email API"]
    SendGrid --> Emails["Transactional Emails"]
    
    subgraph Backend_Security
        Auth
        Rate
        Helmet
        CORS
    end
```

The system has two main components:
- **Frontend**: React 18 SPA served via Create React App, communicating with the backend over HTTP.
- **Backend**: Node.js/Express 5 API server handling authentication, booking logic, email delivery, and database access.

## Key Components

### Frontend (`Frontend/my-app/`)
- React 18 with React Router v6 (client-side routing)
- Axios-based service layer for API communication
- Responsive layout with mobile/desktop variants in the header
- 16 pages including legal documents and a 404 page
- CSS stylesheets organized by page and component

### Backend (`Backend/`)
- Express 5 server listening on port 8080
- JWT-based authentication with token verification middleware
- Rate limiting on all routes, stricter for login/signup
- Helmet security headers for HTTP protection
- CORS restricted to localhost:3000 and production domain
- MySQL database with parameterized queries
- SendGrid integration for transactional emails

### Database
- MySQL 8+ with three tables: `users`, `bookings`, `guest_bookings`
- Schema auto-initialized on startup with `IF NOT EXISTS` safety
- Admin user seeded on first run via environment variables

### Email Service
- SendGrid API for transactional emails (booking confirmations, password resets, welcome emails)
- HTML and plain-text email templates
- Graceful failure handling (booking succeeds even if email fails)

## Frontend Architecture

| Aspect | Implementation |
|--------|---------------|
| Framework | React 18 |
| Routing | React Router v6 (`BrowserRouter` + `Routes`) |
| State | React hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`) |
| API Layer | Axios via `backend_services/` service classes |
| Styling | Per-page and per-component CSS files |
| Auth Storage | `localStorage` (persistent) or `sessionStorage` (session-only) |
| Responsive | Mobile/desktop header variants at 768px breakpoint |

### Page Structure (`Frontend/my-app/src/pages/`)

| Route | Page | Auth Required |
|-------|------|---------------|
| `/` | Home_Page | No |
| `/learn-more` | Learn_More | No |
| `/book-page` | Book_Page | No (guest booking supported) |
| `/find-booking` | Find_Booking_Page | No |
| `/booking-success` | Booking_Success_Page | No |
| `/login` | Login_Page | No |
| `/signup` | Sign-up_Page | No |
| `/forgot-password` | Forgot_Password | No |
| `/reset-password` | Reset_Password | No |
| `/profile-page` | Profile_Page | Yes |
| `/manage-bookings` | Manage_Bookings | Yes (admin) |
| `/manage-users` | Manage_Users | Yes (admin) |
| `/privacy-policy` | Privacy_Policy | No |
| `/terms-conditions` | Terms_Conditions | No |
| `*` (catch-all) | NotFound | No |

## Backend Architecture

### Request Lifecycle

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    Client->>Express: HTTP Request
    Express->>Helmet: Security Headers
    Express->>RateLimiter: Rate Limit Check
    Express->>CORS: Origin Check
    Express->>BodyParser: Parse JSON Body
    Express->>Route: Route Matching
    
    alt Protected Route
        Route->>AuthMiddleware: Verify JWT Token
        AuthMiddleware-->>Route: Decoded User
    end
    
    Route->>Controller: Business Logic
    Controller->>Database: Parameterized Query
    Controller->>SendGrid: Send Email (optional)
    Controller-->>Route: Response Data
    Route-->>Client: JSON Response
```

### Route Modules (`Backend/routes/`)

| File | Endpoints | Auth |
|------|-----------|------|
| `users.js` | Signup, login, profile CRUD, password change, forgot/reset password, admin user management | Mixed |
| `bookings.js` | Create/find/update/cancel bookings, debug routes | Mixed |
| `guest_bookings.js` | Create/find/update/cancel guest bookings, debug routes | Mixed |
| `email_routes.js` | Send booking/guest/user emails, preview, test connection | Mixed |

### Middleware (`Backend/middleware/`)

- **`auth.js`**: JWT verification. Requires `JWT_SECRET` environment variable. Decodes token and attaches `req.user`.

### Key Design Decisions

**Authentication on the backend**: JWTs are created and verified server-side. The frontend stores tokens but never generates or validates them. This ensures the authentication boundary is at the API layer.

**Token hashing for password reset**: Reset tokens are hashed with SHA-256 before storage. If the database is compromised, reset tokens cannot be used without knowing the original token value.

**Rate limiting**: A global limiter (300 requests per 15 minutes) prevents general abuse. An auth-specific limiter (10 attempts per 15 minutes) protects login and signup from brute force.

**Helmet security headers**: Sets HTTP headers to prevent common attacks including XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and other client-side vulnerabilities.

## Database Architecture

```mermaid
erDiagram
    users {
        int id PK
        varchar email UK
        varchar first_name
        varchar last_name
        varchar phone_number
        varchar password_hash
        boolean admin
        varchar reset_token_hash
        timestamp reset_token_expiry
    }
    
    bookings {
        int booking_id PK
        int user_id FK
        varchar room
        date check_in_date
        date check_out_date
        int number_of_guests
        varchar status
        text special_requests
        varchar confirmation_code
        timestamp created_at
    }
    
    guest_bookings {
        int booking_id PK
        varchar guest_first_name
        varchar guest_last_name
        varchar guest_email
        varchar guest_phone_number
        varchar room
        date check_in_date
        date check_out_date
        int number_of_guests
        varchar status
        text special_requests
        varchar confirmation_code
        timestamp created_at
    }
    
    users ||--o{ bookings : has
```

### Key Schema Design Points

- **Passwords** are hashed with bcrypt (10 rounds) — never stored in plain text.
- **Reset tokens** are hashed with SHA-256 before storage (not stored in plain text).
- **Confirmation codes** are randomly generated hex strings (12 chars).
- **Bookings** use soft-delete via `status` field (`cancelled`), not hard deletion.
- **Guest bookings** are stored separately from user bookings, without a FK to `users`.

## Authentication & Authorization

### Flow

1. **Signup**: User submits email + password → password is bcrypt-hashed → user row created → JWT returned
2. **Login**: User submits email + password → password compared with bcrypt hash → if valid, JWT returned
3. **Authenticated requests**: Frontend sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` → `auth.js` middleware verifies JWT → `req.user` populated
4. **Authorization**: Route handlers check `req.user.admin` for admin-only operations

### Security Features

- JWT signed with `JWT_SECRET` (required — server will not start without it)
- Tokens expire after 24 hours
- Guest bookings use temporary 30-minute JWTs scoped to a specific booking
- Login attempt information is not logged at the application level
- Forgot password responses do not reveal whether an email exists

## Security Architecture

### Implemented Safeguards

| Mechanism | What It Protects | Implementation |
|-----------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Helmet** | XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, referrer leakage | `app.use(helmet())` sets ~15 security HTTP headers |
| **Rate Limiting** | Brute force attacks, API abuse | `express-rate-limit` — 300 req/15min global, 10 req/15min on auth endpoints |
| **CORS** | Cross-origin requests from unauthorized domains | Whitelist: `localhost:3000` and `tayandtoscorporations.com` |
| **JWT Authentication** | Unauthorized API access | Token required for protected routes, verified in middleware |
| **Parameterized Queries** | SQL injection | All database queries use `?` placeholders via mysql2 |
| **Password Hashing** | Credential exposure via DB leak | bcrypt with 10 salt rounds |
| **Token Hashing** | Reset token theft via DB leak | SHA-256 hash of reset token stored, not the raw token |
| **Input Validation** | Invalid/malicious input | `validator` library on backend, form validation on frontend |
| **Environment Variables** | Secret exposure in code | Secrets loaded from `.env`, never hardcoded (no fallback values) |
| **Graceful Email Failure** | Booking failure due to email outage | Booking operations succeed even if email sending fails |

- **Footer links** — Both pages are linked from the footer Quick Links section for easy access.

const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const readmePath = path.resolve('README.md');

const content = `# Tay and Tos Accommodation

A full-stack room booking web application for Tay and Tos Accommodation in Ado-Ekiti, Nigeria. Users can browse rooms, create accounts, book rooms, and manage reservations. Administrators can manage users and bookings.

## System Architecture

\`\`\`mermaid
graph TD
    User["Website Visitor"]
    User -->|HTTPS| React["React 18 Frontend (Create React App)"]
    
    React -->|HTTP API Requests| Express["Node.js / Express 5 Backend"]
    Express -->|Auth Middleware| Auth["JWT Authentication"]
    Express -->|Rate Limiting| Rate["express-rate-limit"]
    Express -->|Security Headers| Helmet["helmet"]
    Express -->|CORS| CORS["cors"]
    
    Auth -->|Protected Routes| Routes["Route Handlers"]
    Rate --> Routes
    Helmet --> Routes
    
    Routes --> MySQL["MySQL Database"]
    Routes --> SendGrid["SendGrid Email API"]
    SendGrid --> Emails["Transactional Emails"]
    
    subgraph Backend_Security
        Auth
        Rate
        Helmet
        CORS
    end
\`\`\`

The system has two components: a **React 18 SPA frontend** and a **Node.js/Express 5 API backend**.

## Key Components

### Frontend (\`Frontend/my-app/\`)
- React 18 with React Router v6
- Axios service layer for API communication
- Responsive layout with mobile/desktop header variants
- 16 pages including legal documents and a 404 page
- CSS stylesheets organized by page and component

### Backend (\`Backend/\`)
- Express 5 server on port 8080
- JWT authentication with token verification middleware
- Rate limiting (global + auth-specific)
- Helmet security headers
- CORS restricted to localhost:3000 and production domain
- MySQL with parameterized queries
- SendGrid for transactional emails

### Database
- MySQL 8+ with three tables: \`users\`, \`bookings\`, \`guest_bookings\`
- Schema auto-initialized on startup (\`IF NOT EXISTS\`)
- Admin user seeded on first run

### Email
- SendGrid for transactional emails (booking confirmations, password resets, welcome emails)
- HTML and plain-text templates
- Graceful failure handling (booking succeeds even if email fails)

## Frontend Architecture

| Aspect | Implementation |
|--------|---------------|
| Framework | React 18 |
| Routing | React Router v6 (\`BrowserRouter\` + \`Routes\`) |
| State | React hooks (\`useState\`, \`useEffect\`) |
| API Layer | Axios via \`backend_services/\` service classes |
| Styling | Per-page and per-component CSS files |
| Auth Storage | \`localStorage\` (persistent) or \`sessionStorage\` (session-only) |
| Responsive | Mobile/desktop header variants at 768px breakpoint |

### Routes

| Path | Page | Auth Required |
|------|------|---------------|
| \`/\` | Home | No |
| \`/learn-more\` | Learn More | No |
| \`/book-page\` | Book | No (guest) |
| \`/find-booking\` | Find Booking | No |
| \`/booking-success\` | Booking Success | No |
| \`/login\` | Login | No |
| \`/signup\` | Sign Up | No |
| \`/forgot-password\` | Forgot Password | No |
| \`/reset-password\` | Reset Password | No |
| \`/profile-page\` | Profile | Yes |
| \`/manage-bookings\` | Manage Bookings | Admin |
| \`/manage-users\` | Manage Users | Admin |
| \`/privacy-policy\` | Privacy Policy | No |
| \`/terms-conditions\` | Terms | No |
| \`*\` | 404 Not Found | No |

## Backend Architecture

### Request Lifecycle

\`\`\`
Request
  |-- Helmet (security headers)
  |-- Rate Limiter (abuse prevention)
  |-- CORS (origin validation)
  |-- Body Parser (JSON parsing)
  |-- Route Matching
      |-- [Auth Middleware] (if protected)
      |-- Controller Logic
          |-- Database Query
          |-- [Email Send]
  |-- JSON Response
\`\`\`

### Route Modules

| File | Endpoints | Auth |
|------|-----------|------|
| \`routes/users.js\` | Signup, login, profile CRUD, password change, forgot/reset password, admin user management | Mixed |
| \`routes/bookings.js\` | Create/find/update/cancel bookings, debug | Mixed |
| \`routes/guest_bookings.js\` | Create/find/update/cancel guest bookings | Mixed |
| \`routes/email_routes.js\` | Send emails, preview, test connection | Mixed |

### Key Design Decisions

**Authentication is server-side only.** JWTs are created and verified by the backend. The frontend stores tokens but never generates or validates them. This keeps the authentication boundary at the API layer.

**Password reset tokens are hashed.** The SHA-256 \`hashToken()\` utility (from \`utils/securityUtils.js\`) is used before storing reset tokens in the database. If the database is compromised, reset tokens cannot be reused.

**Rate limiting protects auth endpoints.** Login and signup are limited to 10 attempts per 15 minutes per IP, preventing brute force attacks.

## Database Schema

\`\`\`
users
  id (PK), email (UK), first_name, last_name, phone_number,
  password_hash, admin, reset_token (hashed), reset_token_expiry
  |-- has many bookings

bookings
  booking_id (PK), user_id (FK -> users), room, check_in_date,
  check_out_date, number_of_guests, status, special_requests,
  confirmation_code, created_at

guest_bookings
  booking_id (PK), guest_first_name, guest_last_name, guest_email,
  guest_phone_number, room, check_in_date, check_out_date,
  number_of_guests, status, special_requests,
  confirmation_code, created_at
\`\`\`

### Schema Design Points
- Passwords: bcrypt hashed (10 rounds)
- Reset tokens: SHA-256 hashed before storage
- Confirmation codes: 12-char random hex strings
- Bookings use soft-delete via \`status = 'cancelled'\`
- Guest bookings stored separately from user bookings

## Security Architecture

| Mechanism | What It Protects | Location |
|-----------|-----------------|----------|
| Helmet | XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, referrer leakage | \`server.js\` — \`app.use(helmet())\` |
| Rate Limiting | Brute force, API abuse | \`server.js\` — 300/15min global, 10/15min auth |
| CORS | Unauthorized cross-origin requests | \`server.js\` — whitelisted origins |
| JWT | Unauthorized API access | \`middleware/auth.js\` |
| Parameterized Queries | SQL injection | All \`pool.query(sql, params)\` calls |
| Password Hashing | Credential exposure via DB leak | bcrypt, 10 rounds |
| Token Hashing | Reset token theft via DB leak | SHA-256 before storage |
| Input Validation | Invalid/malicious input | \`validator\` library + frontend validation |
| Environment Variables | Secret exposure in code | \`.env\` with no fallbacks |
| Graceful Email Failure | Booking failure due to email outage | try/catch around email sends |

## Privacy & Legal

- **Privacy Policy**: \`/privacy-policy\` — data collection, third-party services (SendGrid), data retention, user rights
- **Terms & Conditions**: \`/terms-conditions\` — booking policies, user conduct, liability, governing law

npm install

### Database
The backend creates the database and tables automatically on startup. No manual migration steps needed.

### Access

A full-stack room booking web application for Tay and Tos Accommodation in Ado-Ekiti, Nigeria.

## System Architecture

Components: React 18 SPA (frontend) + Node.js/Express 5 API (backend) + MySQL (database) + SendGrid (email).

The frontend communicates with the backend over HTTP API requests.

## Frontend Architecture

Framework: React 18 with React Router v6
API Layer: Axios via backend_services/
Styling: Per-page and per-component CSS
Auth Storage: localStorage or sessionStorage

Routes: / (Home), /login, /signup, /book-page, /find-booking, /profile-page, /manage-users, /manage-bookings, /learn-more, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /booking-success, /privacy-policy, /terms-conditions, * (404)

## Backend Architecture

Route modules: users.js, bookings.js, guest_bookings.js, email_routes.js
Middleware: auth.js (JWT), helmet, rate-limit, cors
Request lifecycle: Request -> Helmet -> Rate Limiter -> CORS -> Body Parser -> Route -> [Auth] -> Controller -> Database/Email -> Response

## Database

MySQL with 3 tables: users, bookings, guest_bookings
Passwords: bcrypt hashed (10 rounds)
Reset tokens: SHA-256 hashed before storage
Confirmation codes: 12-char random hex strings

## Security

Helmet: XSS/clickjacking protection (server.js)
Rate Limiting: 300/15min global, 10/15min auth endpoints
CORS: Whitelisted origins only
JWT: Server-side token verification (middleware/auth.js)
Parameterized Queries: All SQL queries
Password Hashing: bcrypt
Token Hashing: SHA-256 for reset tokens
Input Validation: validator library

## Privacy & Legal

Privacy Policy: /privacy-policy
Terms and Conditions: /terms-conditions
Both linked from footer. Review with legal professional before production.

## Environment Variables

Required: DB_HOST, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET, SENDGRID_API_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD
Optional: DB_PORT, PORT, FROM_EMAIL, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PHONE, FRONTEND_URL
See Backend/.env.example

## Local Development

1. Backend: cd Backend && cp .env.example .env && npm install && npm run dev
2. Frontend: cd Frontend/my-app && npm install && npm start
3. Access: http://localhost:3000

## Project Structure

Backend/: config/, controllers/, middleware/, routes/, sevices/, templates/, utils/, server.js, db.js, setup.sql
Frontend/my-app/: public/ (index.html, robots.txt), src/ (pages/, components/, backend_services/, images/, videos/, App.js)

## Testing

No meaningful test suite exists.

## Troubleshooting

Backend wont start: Check JWT_SECRET and ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env
Database error: Verify MySQL is running and .env credentials
CORS error: Add origin to allowedOrigins in server.js

## Future Improvements

Add email verification, account deletion, migration system, tests.
Technical debt: sevices/ typo, sqlite3 in package.json, hardcoded pricing, no structured logging.
